newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiwa Sec says may post loss in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa Sec says may post loss in 1996/97.

text.p: Daiwa Securities Co Ltd said on Monday it may post losses in the current business year to March 31 after providing aid to its finance affiliate and amid the current weakness of the stock market.

Daiwa Securities managing director Takeshi Nojima told reporters that the firm, Japan's second-biggest broker, still plans to sell equities held for long-term investment, partly to cover 120 billion yen in financial aid to its affiliate Daiwa Finance Co Ltd.

"We still hope to post a profit, but it is very tough," Nojima said. He said there was a possibility of red ink in the broker's earnings figures for 1996/97, as the current vulnerable condition of the stock market meant it was difficult to sell equities to the extent that it had originally planned.
Daiwa Securities said last November that it would provide 120 billion yen in financial aid to Daiwa Finance by posting an extraordinary loss of that amount in the current business year.

Nojima said that to deal with an expected fall in the broker's capital safety ratio from 281 percent at the end of September 1996, it planned to procure subordinated loans which could be counted as part of its capital and to trim its assets, including sales of equities holdings.
The capital safety ratio is the ratio of net capital to latent profit on securities holdings against risk assets and possible losses from securities business.
Industry sources said if Daiwa Securities extended the financial aid, it could see its capital safety ratio fall by around 100 percent.
Nojima declined to comment on the size of subordinated loans which Daiwa Securities would make.

The mass financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Monday that Japan's "Big Four" brokerages are set to make subordinated loans worth between 50 billion to 100 billion yen each by the end of March.
